lines.line: The biggest fans of AI songs are bots.
lines.frame0: AI SONGS' BIGGEST FANS ARE BOTS
lines.emotion: Amused disbelief that turns into suspicion. Everyone assumes a flood of AI songs means somebody wants them; picturing the 'fans' as rows of bots with headphones is funny and a little creepy, and it raises a question a normal person can't answer: why would bots play songs at all?
lines.backing: FL 2.4 (Deezer: up to 85% of plays on fully AI tracks were fake in 2025, depending on the month; the row's fact: most of their plays were fake), FL 2.3 (AI gets 1-3% of all plays), FL 2.5 (fake plays are the main reason AI songs get uploaded), the Never-say table's own 'say instead' ('Real people barely play them. Bots do.'), FL 4.10 (Smith's bot plays). Scope per FL 8.4: the second line says 'on one app' and dates the 85% to 2025; FL 5.13 (plenty of people like some AI music) stays in as the fairness beat.
lines.payoff: The end answers why bots would be fans: streaming pays out of a shared monthly pot split by each track's share of the plays, so every fake play that slips past the filters shaves a little off every real artist's slice (caught ones are stripped out, and nobody knows how many get through).

lines.line: His AI songs got billions of plays, and he got 18 months.
lines.frame0: BILLIONS OF PLAYS. 18 MONTHS IN PRISON.
lines.emotion: Whiplash: 'billions of plays' sounds like a superstar and '18 months' sounds like a crook, so the gap demands an explanation, with a jolt of justice on top; it is one real person, not a plural headline.
lines.backing: FL 1.8 and 4.9 (Michael Smith, sentenced 2026-10-06 to 18 months; forfeits $8,091,843.64), FL 4.10 (prosecutors: 'hundreds of thousands' of AI songs played 'billions' of times by up to 10,000 bot accounts at once; on screen with a 'prosecutors say' credit, and 'over a billion' is the floor), FL 4.11 (his own email: 'a TON of content with small amounts of Streams'), FL 7.10 (no AI tool named or drawn). FL 4.14-4.15 and 8.6: never 'he stole $8 million from artists'; his lawyers' denial gets its line.
lines.payoff: We show the plays came from his own bots and why that's a crime: streaming pays from a shared pot split by plays, so fake plays that slip past the filters (his did, for years) shrink every real artist's slice; the apps now strip out the fakes they catch, but nobody knows how many still get through.

lines.line: An AI song nobody hears can still make money.
lines.frame0: AI SONGS NOBODY HEARS CAN MAKE MONEY
lines.emotion: Unfairness wrapped in curiosity: it breaks the rule everyone takes for granted (no listeners, no money), and the instant follow-up is 'whose money?', which is exactly where real artists come in.
lines.backing: FL 3.1-3.3 (no per-play rate; one shared pot per country per month, split by share of plays), FL 3.7 (more plays in the pot, smaller slices for everyone else), FL 2.4 (most plays on fully AI tracks were fake in 2025, on one app), FL 4.10 (Smith took in $14M+ from bot plays on AI songs over 7 years before he was charged). 'Can', never 'does': caught fakes earn nothing (FL 4.1-4.2, 4.4), most AI tracks never reach Spotify's 1,000-plays-a-year pay line (FL 3.9-3.10), and how much slips through is unknown (FL 8.2).
lines.payoff: We show how: bots play it on repeat, the app splits a shared pot by each track's share of plays, so if those fake plays slip past the filters they take a slice of the same pot that pays real artists, leaving every real slice a little thinner.

lines.line: Somebody's playing all these AI songs, and it's probably not you.
lines.frame0: BOTS PLAY THE AI SONGS YOU DON'T
lines.emotion: A personal itch: people worry they're being fed AI songs without knowing ('can I even tell?'), and 'it's probably not you' flips that worry into a slightly eerie mystery about their own app: then who is? The 'you' lands as a relief, never an accusation.
lines.backing: FL 2.3-2.4 (AI tracks get 1-3% of one app's plays, and up to 85% of those were fake in 2025), FL 3.10 (on Spotify, likely-AI tracks are 10x likelier to fall under the 1,000-play line), FL 2.6 and 1.1 (both apps keep AI slop out of recommendations), FL 5.1 (the blind-test worry it flips, said as 'in a blind test'), FL 3.11 (your fee goes into the shared pot). It never says bots play the viewer's playlist (Never-say): the frame says bots play the songs the viewer doesn't.
lines.payoff: The answer is bots, playing them for a share of the same monthly pot your fee goes into, so the fake plays that slip past the filters leave every real artist's slice a little thinner while you never hear a note.

lines.line: If real people barely play AI songs, why are there so many?
lines.frame0: AI SONGS: FEW LISTENERS, LOTS OF BOTS
lines.emotion: Plain puzzlement: it breaks basic logic (people make what people want), and a normal viewer can't answer it, so they stay for the answer; it is a question to the viewer, not a lecture.
lines.backing: FL 2.3-2.4 (real people barely play them: the fact lock's own 'say instead'), FL 2.1 and 1.6 (nearly 90,000 a day on one app; 42M+ flagged), FL 2.8-2.9 (cheap to make; unlimited uploads for about $25 a year), FL 2.5 (one app says fake plays are the main reason they get uploaded). Spotify's 50M stays out of the 'who are they for' logic (FL 8.10).
lines.payoff: The answer is that many are uploaded for bots to play: the pot is split by each track's share of plays, so cheap songs plus fake plays can grab a slice if they slip past the filters, and that slice comes out of every real artist's share.

lines.line: Nearly half of one app's uploads are AI, and hardly anyone listens.
lines.frame0: NEARLY HALF THE UPLOADS. 1-3% OF PLAYS.
lines.emotion: The jolt of a huge number set against a tiny one: 'half' feels like a takeover, 'hardly anyone listens' undercuts it, and the mismatch makes you ask what the songs are for.
lines.backing: FL 2.2 (44% of daily uploads by April 2026: 'nearly half'), FL 2.1 (over half on peak days in June 2026, nearly 90,000 a day), FL 2.3 (1-3% of plays), FL 8.4 ('one app'; the frame carries a small 'one app, 2026' credit). It never says half of all music (Never-say).
lines.payoff: The plays they do get were mostly fake (up to 85% in 2025, same app), and since the pot is split by share of plays, the fakes that slip past the filters thin every real artist's slice.

lines.line: One app says most AI songs are uploaded for bots to play.
lines.frame0: MOST AI SONG UPLOADS ARE FOR BOTS
lines.emotion: Indignant disbelief: songs exist to be listened to, so songs uploaded for machines to 'listen' to sounds absurd, like someone gaming the system, and you want to know who gets paid.
lines.backing: FL 2.5 (Deezer: 'Generating fake streams continue to be the main purpose for uploading AI-generated music'; safe wording 'One app says most AI songs are uploaded to farm fake plays'), FL 2.4 (up to 85% of their plays fake in 2025), FL 4.11 (Smith's plan in his own words). Always 'uploaded', never 'made': most songs AI apps make never get uploaded (FL 2.8). The frame carries a small 'one app says' credit (FL 8.4).
lines.payoff: We show why bots are worth it: the pot is split by each track's share of plays, so fake plays that slip past the filters thin every real artist's slice, which is why the apps strip out every fake they catch and why the ones they miss matter.

lines.line: On one app, up to 85% of AI song plays were fake.
lines.frame0: AI SONG PLAYS: UP TO 85% FAKE
lines.emotion: Shock at a big, specific number: 'fake plays' is a scam anyone understands at once, and 'up to 85%' makes it feel organized, so you want to know who fakes them and who pays.
lines.backing: FL 2.4 (Deezer: 'up to 85% of these streams were fraudulent in 2025, depending on the month'; 'up to' and the year kept per the Never-say row; the frame carries a small 'one app, 2025' credit), FL 2.3, FL 8.4. The next beat gives the platforms' side: caught fakes get stripped out of the pot (FL 4.1-4.2).
lines.payoff: We show who fakes them and why: the pot is split by each track's share of plays, so the fake plays that slip past the filters (caught ones are stripped out) shave a bit off every real artist's slice, by an amount nobody has measured.
